findings.text: 外部 idempotency ledger 拒绝 stale epoch
findings.verdict: NO SUBJECT -- and worse than absent (sharpened 2026-09-06)
findings.evidence: `idempotencyLedger` and `idempotency ledger` occur 0 times anywhere in packages/. What P4-07 delivers is `checkFencing`, which refuses a token whose epoch is not the item's current one -- a LEASE-level authority check. An idempotency ledger answers a different question: 'have I already applied this effect?'. The nearest thing in the repository is P4-06's message-bus dedup, which belongs to another epic and is not consulted here.
findings.whyItWasMissed: must[0], must[1] and must[2] are all lease/heartbeat/fencing and were built together; must[3] names a component OUTSIDE that cluster. No declared file pointed at it, so neither pre-flight question reached it -- exactly BLOCKED-101's blind spot, in an epic already ACCEPTED.
findings.status: P4-07 is ACCEPTED. Reported for a maintainer decision; not silently reopened.
findings.sharpenedByDelegate: My report said 'idempotency ledger' occurs 0 times, which is true and insufficient -- a mechanism's NAME is not the only evidence of its existence, the trap I had just caught five times in this same audit. Searching by concept instead: `IdempotencyKey` appears 14 times and `idempotencyKey` 18. But following them settles it the other way: both live ONLY in packages/action/action-manifest -- declared in types.ts, computed in canonicalize.ts, exercised by that package's own test. NO consumer anywhere. The key is minted and canonicalized; nothing ever uses it to REFUSE a replay.
findings.whyThisIsWorseThanEmpty: An absent mechanism is honest. Here the system mints idempotency keys, so a future reader finds an `IdempotencyKey` type and a canonicalizer and reasonably concludes deduplication is wired. Identical to P4-09's nesting: machinery present, types present, no call site -- and the part that exists is precisely enough to mislead. Third occurrence of this shape in one session.

findings.text: 将协议 schema 生成物纳入 release evidence 和 golden compatibility fixtures
findings.evidence: The real gap is narrower and harder: EVERY assertion is RELATIVE -- a fingerprint compared against another fingerprint -- and none is ABSOLUTE. Verified: zero 64-hex literals in packages/sdk/protocol/src or /tests. So the suite catches 'this surface differs from that one' and cannot catch 'the ALGORITHM changed', which is the single thing a golden fixture exists for and exactly what must[4] asks for. The release-evidence half is separately absent: `schema` occurs 0 times in scripts/release/collect-evidence.mjs (341 lines), so no protocol schema artifact enters an evidence package.
findings.secondaryFinding: The self-equality assertion is BLOCKED-098's shape: it executes, reports as covered, and can never distinguish any two implementations.
findings.status: P8-01 is ACCEPTED. Reported for a maintainer decision.
findings.correctionToMyOwnReport: My first report called the fingerprint suite BLOCKED-098's shape -- a guard with nothing to decide. THAT WAS WRONG, and wrong in the direction that misdirects the repair. The suite DOES discriminate: reordering a surface keeps the fingerprint (line 149), a version bump changes it (157), an added method changes it (165), a new resource type changes it (169), and moving a name between the method and event kinds changes it (184). A fingerprint function returning a constant would redden four of those. Only line 138's `f(x) === f(x)` is a tautology.
findings.whyTheCorrectionMatters: Read as an 098, the next person deletes line 138 -- a tidy-up that leaves the actual gap untouched. Read correctly, the repair is to ADD a case pinning a fingerprint VALUE. Diagnosis and defect are different things, and I had just written that a false defect 'sends someone to fix what is not broken' -- then produced one, in the diagnosis rather than in the probe.

adopted.name: @pnpm/lockfile.fs
adopted.reason: The authoritative integrity for an installed package is in pnpm-lock.yaml — 1299 real sha512- values on this tree — not in each package's manifest. The hand-written path invented `dsh.provenance.integrity`, a field nothing writes, so every lock entry records the `unavailable:` marker and the boot comparison is structurally inert (BLOCKED-135). Adopting the lockfile reader is what gives must[0]'s `integrity` a real value. Step-3 re-verification on this tree: ESM (`type: module`), engines `>=22.13` which the repository's `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` satisfies.

adopted.name: ssri
adopted.reason: Parses and compares Subresource Integrity strings, which is the format pnpm-lock.yaml records. Hand-comparing `sha512-...` strings byte-for-byte works only while the algorithm and encoding never vary; ssri is the maintained implementation of that comparison. Step-3 re-verification: v13.0.1 pinned deliberately, NOT the latest v14. v14's engines are `^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0`, which EXCLUDES part of this repository's declared range (22.19-22.22.1 and 24.0-24.14); adopting it would silently narrow the Node versions dsh supports. v13.0.1's `^20.17.0 || >=22.9.0` covers the whole range. CommonJS, which is fine for a dependency — the ESM-only rule governs this repository's own modules, and 19 of 36 sampled dependencies are already CJS.

adopted.name: write-file-atomic
adopted.reason: `writeLockAtomically` hand-rolls writeFileSync + renameSync with no fsync, and it duplicates this repository's own `@deepseek-ai/dsh-atomic-write`, whose source already carries `TODO(settings-atomic-durability): Use a replacement that fsyncs the file`. One adoption closes the duplication and the recorded TODO together, which is the case AGENTS.md's dependencies-over-hand-rolling rule is written for: it genuinely deletes owned code rather than adding a layer. Step-3 re-verification: v7.0.1 pinned for the same reason as ssri — v8 carries the same narrowed engines and would drop supported Node versions. CommonJS, which is acceptable for a dependency.
adopted.landsIn: P supersession, alongside dsh-atomic-write's own TODO

methodCorrections.lesson: A mechanism's NAME is not the only evidence of its existence.
methodCorrections.detail: I applied 'read, do not count' to five probes that returned ZERO and correctly found the subjects. Then I reported P4-07's absence from a single name search. The delegate searched by CONCEPT and found the type; following it to its consumers is what settled the question -- in the same direction, but for a better reason and with a sharper finding.

methodCorrections.lesson: A wrong diagnosis is a false defect, and false defects send people to fix what is not broken.
methodCorrections.detail: The P8-01 miscall would have produced a deletion instead of an addition. The audit's credibility rests on 2 findings out of 19 rather than 7; a wrong diagnosis damages that the same way a wrong probe would.
